description: Persist Workflow OpenCode turn input and normalized runtime events in the associated AgentSession, then close each recorded turn as completed or failed without allowing best-effort Session reporting to control Workflow completion.

tasks.title: Record Workflow OpenCode turn transcripts
tasks.description: Add a Workflow-local, turn-scoped event reporter to `mohist/opencode` after physical AgentSession binding resolution, and make canonical AgentSession input acceptance a deterministic transcript boundary. Enqueue the exact composed prompt as `session.input`, forward normalized observer events in production order, isolate bounded upload failures from the Action result, and flush prior pending transcript data before the Session grain accepts a later input.
acceptanceCriteria: For a Workflow Action with a resolved `(projectId, workflowRunId, sessionName)` target and current physical binding, the first attempted runtime-event report is `session.input` containing the exact composed prompt, `kind: task`, `source: workflow`, `role: user`, and the current `runtimeSessionId`; the request envelope retains `workId`, `workType`, `stage`, and `runtimeSessionId`.

`opencodeAction` passes a synchronous `RuntimeTurnObserver.onEvent` to `OpenCodeRuntime.runTurn` and forwards normalized `message.delta`, `reasoning.delta`, `tool_call.started`, `tool_call.updated`, `tool_call.completed`, `usage.updated`, and `model.resolved` events without reprojecting SDK payloads in the Action.

One turn-scoped promise chain serializes input and projected event uploads in observation order, waits for queued attempts to settle before returning, and records whether input was accepted; if input is rejected, later activity and close reports for that turn are skipped, while a rejection after accepted input does not poison later event attempts.

Upload timeout or rejection logs the WorkflowRun, work ID, session name, event type, and error without logging prompt or event payload content; it does not prevent prompt submission, change a successful Action to failed, replace an OpenCode failure, retry the request, or write a local fallback. Request cancellation is independent of an already-aborted runtime signal and bounded so stalled reporting cannot retain the Action indefinitely.

Focused runner specs using a fake OpenCode runtime/SDK client and recording ServerConnection verify exact input and event ordering, assistant and reasoning deltas, complete tool lifecycle with input/output/error, usage and model observations, final-response reconciliation without duplicate content, suppression of orphan reports after input rejection, and continuation after a later event rejection without real network, process, filesystem, or wall-clock time.

Before `AgentSessionGrain` accepts a `session.input` while prior transcript data is pending, it invokes the existing persistence path; only a successful flush allows the new input to reach `TranscriptAccumulator`, while a failed flush rejects the new input and retains the prior pending accumulator state for retry.

Session grain coverage appends two input/activity sequences on the same logical and physical session back-to-back without advancing fake time or manually flushing between inputs, performs one final flush for observation, and proves two turns retain their own prompts and parts in order.

A transcript-store failure triggered by the second input leaves the first pending turn retryable and does not overwrite its prompt or append the second input; focused coverage retries persistence deterministically without scheduler waits or real time.
Existing `agent-job-executor.spec.ts` transcript, ordering, and upload-failure cases pass unchanged and prove AgentJob still uses its generic AgentSession route with existing content semantics.
No server endpoint, request DTO, database schema, persisted AgentSession model, Web component, retry loop, outbox, or external dependency is added or changed.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner`, `npm test -w packages/runner`, and `npm test` pass with no Git-visible generated changes.
tasks.output: Workflow turn transcript reporting in `packages/runner/src/actions/opencode.ts`, a deterministic input boundary in `packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/Grains/AgentSessionGrain.cs`, focused runner and Session grain specs, and unchanged AgentJob regression coverage.
tasks.notes: Keep the reporter local to the Workflow OpenCode adapter; do not extract or migrate AgentJob reporting and do not move source-specific input policy into `OpenCodeRuntime`. The server fence is cross-source because `session.input` is the canonical turn delimiter, but it changes no API or stored model. This task is independently usable: Workflow session pages receive distinct input/runtime turns even before terminal convergence is added.

tasks.title: Converge Workflow AgentSession state after each turn
tasks.description: Extend the Workflow turn reporter from T-001 so `opencodeAction` enqueues exactly one `session.closed` after all observed and reconciled runtime events, then settles the queue before returning the unchanged Action result. Map runtime success to completed and runtime failure, interruption, or timeout to failed; verify through the existing Workflow route that consecutive turns remain distinct and the latest accepted close drives session reads.
acceptanceCriteria: A successful `runTurn` result whose input was accepted enqueues exactly one final `session.closed` report with `status: completed`, `exitCode: 0`, and the current `runtimeSessionId` after every prior projected-event attempt for that turn; a rejected input produces no close.

A failed, interrupted, or timed-out `runTurn` result whose input was accepted enqueues exactly one final `session.closed` report with `status: failed`, `exitCode: 1`, `failureReason` equal to the original runtime error message, and the current `runtimeSessionId`; a rejected input produces no close and does not alter the runtime failure.

The close uses the existing Workflow runtime-events target and serialized queue; a close timeout or rejection is logged once, is not retried or locally persisted, and cannot change a runtime success or replace/obscure the original runtime failure.

Two sequential Workflow OpenCode turns that reuse one logical and physical AgentSession each record a new input and one close; event order is `input/activity/close` per turn and the later accepted close is the latest terminal observation.

Focused runner specs cover completed close, failed close, close-after-reconciled-events ordering, close upload rejection on both runtime success and failure, bounded reporting after an aborted runtime signal, and two-turn session reuse using fakes and deterministic timers/signals.

A focused server spec opens and attaches a Workflow AgentSession, posts two input/assistant/tool/close sequences through the existing Workflow runtime-events route with no intervening time advance or flush, performs one final deterministic flush for observation, and verifies two transcript turns plus the latest completed/failed status through Workflow session reads.
Existing AgentJob executor specs remain unchanged and green; no runner-generated `session.closed` is added to the AgentJob path because AgentJob completion remains its terminal authority.
No endpoint, request DTO, database schema, persisted model, Web, retry, outbox, or historical transcript backfill change is introduced.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/runner`, `npm test -w packages/runner`, and `npm test` pass with no Git-visible generated changes.
tasks.output: Terminal `session.closed` reporting and multi-turn convergence in the Workflow OpenCode adapter, with focused runner specs and a Workflow runtime-events route persistence/status spec.
tasks.notes: Consumes T-001's serialized reporter; do not close from `OpenCodeRuntime` or server TaskRun reporting. The Session close is a runtime fact only and must not advance or adjudicate Workflow work. The dependency graph is T-001 -> T-002 and is acyclic.
